chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali Al-Washa, from Abu Al-Hasan Al-Rida (peace be upon him), said:

I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: 'When a man dies and upon him is the fasting of two consecutive months due to an illness, then upon him is that he should give in charity for the first month, and make up the second month.'

key_terms.يَتَصَدَّقَ: He should give in charity (feed the poor)

ai.seo_question: What is the difference in expiation for the first and second month of consecutive fasts when a person dies with outstanding fasts?
ai.summary: This ruling from Imam al-Rida (AS) clarifies the distinction between the expiation (kaffarah) of missed Ramadan fasts, which requires feeding the poor, and the mere making up (qada') of other consecutive fasts, which requires fasting. It reflects the Shia jurisprudential view that the heavy penalty of feeding sixty poor people is specific to the missed fasts of Ramadan due to illness or old age, whereas other consecutive fasts do not carry this specific financial burden upon death. This distinction highlights the precision in applying Quranic verses to different categories of obligatory fasts.
